item.title: AI giants 'not being nearly careful enough,' warns outgoing OpenAI safety engineer
item.description: Days after President Donald Trump signed a voluntary pact with artificial intelligence giants, a former OpenAI worker said his industry needs the same safeguards as nuclear power or aviation.

item.title: Pakistan vs. Afghanistan: From allies and neighbors to war
item.description: For years, Pakistan supported the Taliban in Afghanistan. But now Pakistan is bombing its neighbor. How the former allies became adversaries and why negotiations keep failing.

item.title: UK remands 2 Iranians over alleged antisemitic terror plot
item.description: The pair were arrested on the eve of Yom Kippur and later charged with plotting to attack Jewish targets in Manchester.

item.title: Flydubai co-pilot attempted 'terrorist attack,' UAE says
item.description: The man, who stabbed his fellow pilot on an Israel-bound Flydubai flight, was reportedly barred from flying in his native Oman over security concerns.

item.title: Morocco's first female head of government: Symbol or real reform?
item.description: Fatima Zahra Mansouri has been chosen as Morocco's first female prime minister. Is her appointment a kind of symbolism, to show Morocco in a positive light? Or could Mansouri bring genuine changes for Moroccan women?

item.title: Bosnia and Herzegovina is still shaped by war, separatism, EU ambitions
item.description: Bosnia and Herzegovina is governed by a system established after the Bosnian war — more than 30 years ago. Ethnic divisions, a complex administration and European integration all shape the country's political reality.

item.title: Australia: Car crashes into rugby fans, 10 injured
item.description: The driver has been identified as an 18-year-old man who is said to have been "revving" when he lost control of his car.

item.title: Spain's parliament rejects housing bill as protests continue
item.description: Spain's minority government suffered defeat in parliament as it tried to push through a pair of emergency measures aimed at making housing more affordable. A pensioner's eviction and protests led to the bid.

item.title: Iran accused of blocking SIM cards, digital access to silence dissent
item.description: DW has spoken with several Iranians who say their SIM cards, bank access and online accounts were blocked until they deleted critical content or pledged to stop activism.

item.title: Argentina launches cash-for-citizenship scheme
item.description: Investors seeking the fastest but most costly route to Argentine citizenship can choose between a non-refundable gift of $350,000, or buying a government bond for $800,000, if they think that will pay off in the end.

item.title: Growing fear of war in the Horn of Africa after Eritrea cuts ties with Ethiopia
item.description: The Tigray conflict is no longer just a domestic issue. As Ethiopia, Eritrea and Egypt trade accusations, the African Union (AU) urges restraint. Is the Horn of Africa hurtling toward a wider regional crisis?

item.title: North and South Korea trade accusations over landmines that injured three soldiers
item.description: A mine blast that injured three South Korean soldiers has renewed scrutiny of North Korea's actions along the border and raised questions about its strategic goals.

item.title: This island in Kiribati could be the key to solve the Amelia Earhart mystery
item.description: Nearly 90 years after US aviator Amelia Earhart vanished over the Pacific, a new expedition to the remote island of Nikumaroro hopes a lagoon anomaly could finally reveal the fate of her missing aircraft.
